claim: In the on-demand modes, data ingested into Kinesis Data Streams is billed per GB written. It is calculated as the number of records multiplied by the size of each record rounded up to the nearest 1 KB (1,024 bytes), so a 4.5 KB record counts as 5 KB.
question: How does Kinesis Data Streams bill data ingested, and how is record size rounded?

values.display: rounded up to the nearest 1 KB

qualifiers.condition: each record is rounded up to the nearest 1 KB (1,024 bytes)

evidence.quote: Data-In: The data ingested into Kinesis Data Streams is billed per GB written into your data stream. This is calculated as the number of data records you send to the service, multiplied by the size of each record rounded up to the nearest 1 KB (1,024 bytes). For example, if your data records are 4.5 KB each, Kinesis Data Streams will count each record as 5 KB of data ingested.

claim: In the on-demand modes, data retrieved from Kinesis Data Streams is billed per GB read, as the number of records retrieved multiplied by the size of each record. No rounding factor applies, so a 4.5 KB record counts as 4.5 KB.
question: How does Kinesis Data Streams bill data retrieved, and is record size rounded?

evidence.quote: Data-Out: The data retrieved from Kinesis Data Streams is billed per GB read from a data stream. This is calculated as the number of records retrieved multiplied by the size of each record. There is no rounding factor applied for this calculation. If your data records are 4.5 KB each, Kinesis Data Streams will count each one as 4.5 KB of data egressed.

claim: All data ingested into Kinesis Data Streams is stored for 24 hours by default, with no additional charges for that storage.
question: Is the default 24-hour storage on Kinesis Data Streams charged separately?

evidence.quote: All the data ingested into Kinesis Data Streams is stored for 24 hours by default, and there are no additional charges.

claim: In provisioned mode pricing, a PUT Payload Unit is counted in 25 KB payload chunks of a record. A 5 KB record contains one unit, a 45 KB record contains two units, and a 1 MB record contains 40 units.
question: What is a PUT Payload Unit in Kinesis Data Streams provisioned pricing, and how big is it?

values.display: a 1 MB record contains 40 PUT Payload Units

qualifiers.condition: the unit is charged per million PUT Payload Units

evidence.quote: A PUT Payload Unit is counted in 25 KB payload “chunks” that comprise a record. For example, a 5 KB record contains one PUT Payload Unit, a 45 KB record contains two PUT Payload Units, and a 1 MB record contains 40 PUT Payload Units.

claim: In provisioned mode, the shard is the base throughput unit of a Kinesis data stream. You specify the number of shards you need, and you are charged for each shard at an hourly rate.
question: What is the main charge in Kinesis Data Streams provisioned mode?

values.display: charged for each shard at an hourly rate

qualifiers.scope: per shard per hour, provisioned mode

evidence.quote: Shard hour: Shard is the base throughput unit of an Amazon Kinesis data stream. You specify the number of shards needed within your stream based on your throughput requirements. You’re charged for each shard at an hourly rate.

claim: In provisioned mode, extended data retention extends storage from the 24-hour default up to seven days. Once you start it, you are charged an additional rate on each shard hour of the stream.
question: How long does extended retention keep data in provisioned mode, and how is it charged?

values.display: extend the storage up to seven days

qualifiers.condition: retention beyond seven days is long-term retention

evidence.quote: Extended data retention: Kinesis Data Streams stores your data for 24 hours by default. Extended data retention gives you the option to extend the storage up to seven days. Once you start extended data retention, you’re charged for an additional rate on each shard hour incurred by your data stream.

claim: In provisioned mode, long-term data retention lets you store a data stream up to 365 days. You are charged extended retention rates for the first seven days and then a GB-month rate for data stored beyond seven days.
question: What is long-term retention in Kinesis Data Streams and when does it start?

qualifiers.condition: first seven days at extended retention rates

evidence.quote: Long-term data retention: Long-term data retention gives you the option to store your data stream up to 365 days. You’re charged extended data retention rates for the first seven days and then charged a GB-month rate of data stored beyond seven days up to your specified retention period.

claim: In provisioned mode, retrieving data stored beyond seven days with the GetRecords API is charged per GB. Data stored for the 24-hour default or for extended retention up to seven days has no retrieval charge, and retrieval with an enhanced fan-out consumer has no long-term retrieval charge.
question: When is reading old data from Kinesis Data Streams charged separately?

qualifiers.condition: only for GetRecords retrieval of data older than seven days

evidence.quote: Retrieval of long-term retention data: You’re charged a per-GB rate for retrieval of data stored beyond seven days if you are retrieving data using GetRecords API. You’re not charged for retrieval of data stored for the 24-hour default or for extended data retention up to seven days. You’re not charged for long-term data retrieval if enhanced fan-out consumer (SubscribeToShard API) is used.

claim: In provisioned mode, enhanced fan-out gives each consumer its own read throughput per shard of up to 2 MB/second. Consumers that use it incur hourly charges per consumer-shard hour and per GB of data retrieved.
question: What does enhanced fan-out cost in Kinesis Data Streams provisioned mode?

qualifiers.scope: per consumer, per shard, provisioned mode

evidence.quote: Enhanced fan-out: Enhanced fan-out improves read parallelism by providing each data consumer with their own read throughput per shard (up to 2 MB/second). When consumers use enhanced fan-out, they incur hourly charges per consumer-shard hour and per GB of data retrieved.

claim: In On-demand Standard mode, you are charged for each stream in your account at an hourly rate, in addition to the data ingested and retrieved.
question: Does On-demand Standard mode charge per stream as well as per GB?

values.display: each stream operating in the On-demand Standard mode

qualifiers.scope: per stream per hour, On-demand Standard mode
qualifiers.condition: On-demand Advantage removes this fixed charge

evidence.quote: Per-Stream: You’re charged for each stream operating in the On-demand Standard mode in your account at an hourly rate.

claim: In On-demand Advantage mode, pricing is based on data ingested and retrieved with a minimum charge of 25MB/s ingested and 25MB/s retrieved at the account level across all on-demand streams. There is no fixed stream-hour charge and no additional charge for enhanced fan-out.
question: What does On-demand Advantage charge for, and what charges does it remove?

qualifiers.scope: per account, across all on-demand streams
qualifiers.condition: extended retention is an additional charge

evidence.quote: Pricing is based on the volume of data ingested and retrieved, and there is a minimum charge of 25MB/s data ingested and 25MB/s data retrieved at the account level across all on-demand streams. There is no fixed stream-hour charge. There is an additional charges for optional feature Extended Retention (beyond the first 24 hours and up to one years). There is no additional charge for using Enhanced Fan-Out.

claim: In On-demand Advantage mode there is no longer a fixed charge for each stream, and data ingest, data retrieval and extended retention usage across all on-demand streams are at least 60% lower than in On-demand Standard.
question: How much cheaper is On-demand Advantage than On-demand Standard for data usage?

qualifiers.scope: across all on-demand streams in the account
qualifiers.condition: On-demand Advantage is an account-level mode with a minimum usage commitment

evidence.quote: For pricing, there's no longer a fixed charge for each stream. Data ingest, data retrieval, and extended retention usage across all on-demand streams are at least 60% lower than in On-demand Standard.

claim: On-demand Advantage might be best if you have at least 10MB/s of data ingest in aggregate, fan out to more than 2 consumers, use more than 50 streams in an account, or want to set warm throughput for on-demand streams.
question: When does On-demand Advantage fit better than On-demand Standard?

evidence.quote: On-demand Advantage might be best if you have at least 10MB/s of data ingest in aggregate, fanout to more than 2 consumers, use more than 50 streams in an account, or want the capability to set warm throughput for on-demand streams.

claim: Using warm throughput on a Kinesis data stream does not incur any additional cost.

evidence.quote: Using warm throughput does not incur any additional cost.
